concept.name: Mempool
concept.definition: The mempool (memory pool) is each node's local holding area for valid broadcast transactions that have not yet been included in a block; block producers select transactions from it, typically by fee offered.
concept.intuition: It is the public waiting room for transactions — and because everyone can read it, predators can see your trade before it executes.
concept.mechanics: When a user broadcasts a transaction, each receiving node validates it, adds it to its local mempool and gossips it to peers. Validators pick transactions (usually highest priority fee first) when building a block; transactions can linger, be replaced by higher-fee versions, or be dropped. Public visibility of pending transactions enables front-running and sandwich attacks.
concept.failure_modes: Public mempool visibility lets searchers front-run or sandwich pending trades; congestion can leave low-fee transactions pending indefinitely, and private relay channels used to avoid this reintroduce centralization.
concept.misconceptions: The mempool is not a single global queue — each node has its own mempool and they can differ. Inclusion is not FIFO; ordering is at the block builder's discretion and usually fee-driven.
concept.example: A 100 ETH Uniswap buy sits in the mempool for ~12 seconds before inclusion; a sandwich bot sees it, buys the same token in front of it, lets the victim's trade push the price up, and sells immediately after for a profit.

citations.source: Ethereum.org developer docs - Maximal extractable value (MEV)
